mainKeyword: pressure washer for houses and siding
guideTitle: Best Pressure Washers for Houses and Siding (2026)
metaTitle: Best Pressure Washers for House Siding (2026)
metaDescription: Six electric pressure washers for house washing and siding, compared by rated PSI, flow, soap delivery and reach, plus tips to keep water behind panels out.
expertTake: The Greenworks 3000 PSI brushless is the best pick for house washing because its higher flow rinses a wall faster, and the pressure is easy to throttle back for siding. The Westinghouse ePX3100 is the value pick for a typical single-storey house. Anyone with a tall house, brick that needs scrubbing or heavy mildew should plan on a long hose, a soap routine and a ladder-free approach, not just a bigger machine.
introParagraphs: Washing a house is a different job from cleaning a driveway. Siding is thin, laps overlap in a way that lets water run behind them if you spray upward, and the dirt is mostly a thin film of algae, pollen and mildew that comes off with detergent and a gentle rinse rather than raw force.

That favours machines with moderate rated pressure, decent flow to rinse a wall quickly, and a reliable way to apply cleaner at low pressure. A tall target also rewards a longer hose and a lance you can handle without stretching.

products.name: Greenworks 3000 PSI brushless electric pressure washer
products.description:
For house washing, flow does a lot of the work, because a wall is mostly a rinse job after the detergent has done its dwell. The Greenworks lists up to 2.0 GPM with JETTFLOW technology, which the maker says delivers up to 50% more flow for rinsing and reaching higher areas, and states that the pressure and flow figures were verified by an independent lab. That is useful when so many figures on this category are only claims.

The 3000 PSI is far more than siding needs, but a machine that can do 3000 can be throttled back with a wide tip, and the same unit then handles concrete and decks. Against the Westinghouse WPX3000e, it offers higher flow, though the Westinghouse states a lower rated figure honestly. Against the Greenworks 2000, you pay for the brushless motor and the extra reach in rinsing.

For siding, use a 25 or 40 degree tip, keep the lance angled downward, work top to bottom and let the soap dwell without drying. The axial cam pump is not rebuildable, so keep it from running dry and drain it before freezing weather. On a big house, plan the job in sections: soap a manageable area, rinse it before the cleaner dries, then move on, rather than coating the whole house and racing the sun. Early morning or overcast days give you the longest dwell time.
products.bestFor: Whole-house washing where fast rinsing and a margin of power both matter.
pros: Up to 2.0 GPM for fast rinsing
Output claims verified by an independent lab
Brushless motor runs cooler
3000 PSI can be throttled back with wide tips
cons: 2.0 GPM is a maximum, not sustained at full pressure

products.name: Westinghouse WPX3000e induction-motor electric pressure washer
products.description:
The WPX3000e spells out what it does under load: 2600 PSI at 1.1 GPM, about 2,860 cleaning units, with a 3000 PSI and 1.76 GPM peak at different settings. For siding, that rated flow of 1.1 GPM is the number to notice, because it means a wall takes longer to rinse than with the Greenworks.

The heavy-duty induction motor and axial three-piston auto-stop pump are built to be low maintenance, and the induction design tends to run quietly. A 25-foot abrasion-resistant hose with a metal gun and a wand with five quick-connect nozzles come in the box. Against the ePX3500 it gives more rated pressure, at the same sort of flow.

The practical advice for house washing is to use the soap nozzle at low pressure for the detergent pass, let it dwell for several minutes but not dry, and rinse from the top down with a wide tip. Keep the lance low and angled down so water cannot get behind laps. Drain the pump after use. Work with the wind at your back so overspray does not blow onto freshly rinsed siding, and cover nearby plants with a tarp before you start, since detergent runoff can burn tender foliage.
products.bestFor: Owners who want clearly stated working output with a quiet induction motor.
pros: Clear rated output of 2600 PSI at 1.1 GPM
Induction motor runs quiet
25-foot hose and five quick-connect tips
Auto-stop pump saves wear
cons: 1.1 GPM rated flow is slower on large walls
Peak figures of 3000 PSI and 1.76 GPM apply at different settings

products.name: Westinghouse ePX3500 compact electric pressure washer
products.description:
A sensible machine for siding because 2000 PSI at 1.2 GPM is a rated output that needs no throttling for vinyl, and the onboard 20-ounce soap tank means you can apply cleaner at low pressure without extra equipment. It stands 16.5 inches tall, weighs about 19 pounds and has four quick-lock wheels with anti-tipping design, so it follows you around the house.

The braided nylon hose coils easily and resists kinking, a small point that matters when you drag it along a long wall. Compared with the ePX3100 below, this model offers a higher rated pressure, though the flow is almost the same. Against the WPX3000e it is lighter and easier to store, at the price of 600 PSI of rated output.

To care for it, store the hose coiled loosely, drain the pump, and check the quick-connect o-rings. Run detergent only through the soap nozzle setting, flush the tank after use and never leave chemicals sitting in it.
products.bestFor: Single-storey vinyl or painted siding where a light rolling machine and onboard soap are enough.
pros: 2000 rated PSI suits vinyl without throttling
Onboard 20 oz soap tank
Light at about 19 lb with wheels
Braided hose resists kinks
cons: Rated flow of 1.2 GPM means slow rinsing on large walls
Small soap tank needs refills on a big house

products.name: Westinghouse ePX3100 compact electric pressure washer
products.description:
The ePX3100 is the older, plainer sibling of the ePX3500, rated at 1900 PSI and 1.24 GPM, about 2,356 cleaning units. That is a hair higher flow than the ePX3500 and a little less pressure, which is arguably the better balance for rinsing siding.

It shares the 16.5-inch height, 19-pound weight and anti-tipping layout, so it is just as easy to move around a house. At this level it is best for a typical single-storey home where the job is a soap pass and a rinse, not a deep clean on stubborn stains. Compared with the Greenworks 2000, the Westinghouse spells out rated figures, which makes comparison straightforward.

Keep the lance angled down, rinse top to bottom, and use the wide tips. The on-board hose reel is the piece that earns its keep here, since a coiled hose kinks far less on a two-storey wall than a loose one dragged around the house. Before you begin, close windows and doors, check that window screens and weep holes are intact, and tape over any exterior outlets or light fixtures, since a stream can force water into places a garden hose never reaches.
products.bestFor: Typical single-storey houses where a soap pass and a gentle rinse is the whole job.
pros: Rated 1.24 GPM is a touch higher than the ePX3500
Compact, light and anti-tipping
Clearly stated rated output
Good balance of pressure and flow for siding
cons: Lower rated pressure than the ePX3500 and WPX3000e
Not suited to stubborn stains on brick or concrete

products.name: Westinghouse ePX3050 electric washer with foam cannon, 35-ft cord
products.description:
A long 35-foot GFCI cord is the practical advantage here, because a house wash often means moving around a whole building with a single outlet nearby. The low 26-inch cart on 5-inch never-flat wheels follows you around without tipping on uneven ground, and a foam cannon is included for applying cleaner.

Rated at 1800 PSI and 1.2 GPM, it is the gentlest of the Westinghouse set, which suits vinyl and painted wood siding well. The foam cannon coats a wall with clinging cleaner, which gives a long dwell time, though it dilutes through the cannon rather than the downstream injector. Against the ePX3500, you trade a built-in tank for a cannon and a longer cord.

Flush the cannon with clean water after each use so soap does not dry in the orifice, drain the pump and coil the cord loosely. Check the wheels for grit and keep the machine upright when you store it.
products.bestFor: Houses where one outlet must reach the whole wall and a foam cannon helps cleaner dwell.
pros: 35-foot GFCI cord gives reach
Foam cannon for clinging cleaner
Low 26-inch cart on never-flat wheels
1800 rated PSI is gentle on vinyl
cons: Lowest rated pressure of the Westinghouse set
Cannon dilutes cleaner differently than a downstream injector

products.name: Greenworks 2000 PSI electric pressure washer, PWMA rated
products.description:
Greenworks says this unit was rated in accordance with PWMA standards, the industry body's test method, which at least ties the 2000 PSI and 1.2 GPM figures to a common procedure. That works out to about 2,400 cleaning units, in line with the Westinghouse ePX3500.

The maker positions it for medium-duty projects such as patio furniture, grills, walkways and vehicles, and that is a fair description of what it will do on siding too: a soap pass and a gentle rinse on a modest house. Compared with the Greenworks 3000, it is far less powerful and has no brushless motor, but it also costs less and is far easier to control around trim and windows. Against the Westinghouse machines it is plainer, with fewer accessories documented.

Upkeep is minimal, as there is no engine to maintain. With no engine and a short lance, the only routine task is keeping the quick-connect collar clean so tips seat fully under load. Keep a spare pair of quick-connect o-rings in the toolbox, and never leave the machine outdoors over winter.
products.bestFor: Small houses and mixed light cleaning where a standards-rated, no-frills machine is enough.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Siding needs a rinse more than a blast, and flow clears a wall faster. The Greenworks 3000 lists up to 2.0 GPM, while the Westinghouse WPX3000e rates 1.1 GPM and the ePX3100 1.24. If two machines rate the same PSI, the one with more flow cleans a wall faster.

House washing is mostly a detergent job, applied at low pressure and left to dwell. The ePX3500 has a 20-ounce onboard tank, the ePX3050 a foam cannon and most others a downstream injector through the soap nozzle. A foam cannon clings longer on vertical siding.

Use a 25 or 40 degree tip, hold the lance angled downward and never spray upward under laps, which drives water behind the siding. A 0 degree tip can gouge wood and dent aluminum. Work from the top down so dirty water runs over unwashed siding.

Houses are large, so look at hose and cord lengths. The ePX3050 has a 35-foot GFCI cord and the WPX3000e a 25-foot hose. Wheeled carts on never-flat wheels follow you around without tipping on uneven ground.
Westinghouse lists rated output next to peak: 2600 PSI at 1.1 GPM against a 3000 PSI max on the WPX3000e. The Greenworks 3000 claims lab-verified numbers. Prefer machines that state rated output.

Vinyl and painted wood tolerate far less than brick or concrete, and old caulk, window seals and loose paint can be blown off. The ePX3050 at 1800 rated PSI is gentle, while the WPX3000e can do more damage if misused. Test in a hidden spot first.

howWeEvaluated.title: Flow for rinsing
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared rated and claimed flow from 1.1 to 2.0 GPM, since rinsing speed decides how long a wall takes. Higher flow scored better where the figure was credible. We relied on specifications, not bench time.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pressure control
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at rated pressure from 1800 to 3000 PSI and whether a machine can be throttled for siding. Clearly rated machines scored higher. Excess headroom on the Greenworks 3000 is useful because it can be backed off.

howWeEvaluated.title: Detergent delivery
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the 20 oz onboard tank, the foam cannon and injector soap nozzles. Cleaner applied at low pressure with long dwell is the heart of house washing.

howWeEvaluated.title: Reach and handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared hose and cord lengths and cart designs from 19 pounds upward. A 35-foot cord or a stable low cart scored higher for large houses.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership burden
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed upkeep: pump type, winterizing and fitting care. All are low-maintenance electrics, with differences in serviceability.

cards.label: Foam cannon
cards.text: The ePX3050 coats a wall in clinging foam that dwells longer on vertical siding. It needs the cannon filled and rinsed each time.

cards.label: Onboard soap tank
cards.text: The ePX3500 draws cleaner through a downstream injector at low pressure, with less fuss and thinner coverage. It suits quick passes.

howToChoose.note: Take a cannon for mildew-prone siding, and an onboard tank for light seasonal washing.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A reliable way to apply cleaner at low pressure and a machine with enough flow to rinse. Let the cleaner dwell without drying.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The ePX3050 with its foam cannon and the ePX3500 with its tank are set up for soap, and the Greenworks 3000 rinses fastest.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The house is large or tall and you value a fast rinse. The Greenworks 3000 saves time.

cards.label: Save if

faq.q: Is a pressure washer safe for vinyl siding?
faq.a: Yes with a wide 25 or 40 degree tip, downward angle and moderate pressure. Never spray upward under laps, which drives water behind the panels.

faq.q: How much PSI do I need for a house?
faq.a: Moderate pressure is enough: about 1800 to 2600 rated PSI. Flow matters more for rinsing speed.
Usually yes. Mildew and algae are removed mainly by cleaner dwelling on the surface, then rinsed with a gentle stream.

faq.q: Can I clean a second storey from the ground?
faq.a: A long lance can reach a bit, but spraying upward risks water behind laps. For tall walls use an extension pole made for pressure washers or a soft-wash approach.

faq.q: Which tip is best for siding?
faq.a: The 25 or 40 degree tip, with the soap nozzle for detergent. Avoid the 0 degree tip.

faq.q: Will pressure washing damage paint or caulk?
faq.a: It can on old or failing finishes. Test a hidden area first and keep a good distance.
